Method of Attack: Phishing email with malicious document attachment containing macros
Malicious macros drop and execute 'updater.vbs' script creating scheduled task to impersonate Windows update
'updater.vbs' executes two obfuscated PowerShell scripts 'Script.ps1' and 'Temp.ps1'
'Script.ps1' connects to attacker C2 servers, sends victim ID, and awaits AES-256 CBC encrypted commands
'Temp.ps1' decodes commands, executes them, encrypts and uploads results via POST to C2
Commands include data exfiltration, user enumeration, file listing, file and account removal, and RDP client enumeration
Impacted Systems: Windows systems targeted by phishing emails
Government, corporate, and private user systems
Attack Vector: Phishing email with malicious document attachment themed as LinkedIn job application
Indicators of Compromise: PowerShell scripts 'Script.ps1' and 'Temp.ps1' embedded in document
AES-256 CBC encrypted commands sent from C2
